title: Tenant 2FA routes not covered by authenticate
description: authenticate is mounted on /auth/me, /auth/logout, /tenant and /search but not /auth/2fa.
claimed_root_cause: Unauthenticated access to 2FA setup and disable.
reason: Not a vulnerability: without req.auth the handler throws and returns 500 before any read or write. Confirmed as a real functional defect by the owner's npm test run (login-security.test.ts: 500 on POST /auth/2fa/setup), so tenant staff could not enable 2FA. Fixed by adding /auth/2fa to the authenticate mount list in app.ts.

title: Tenant owner can activate paid add-ons without payment
description: POST /tenant/addons/:key/activate grants entitlements (sms, whatsapp, custom domain, storage) with no gateway call, also outside sandbox mode. Entitlements gate operator-funded SMS and WhatsApp delivery. The docs state add-on charging is not wired yet.
claimed_root_cause: Add-on activation is a plain database write with no payment verification.

trace.description: active add-on grants merged into limits
sms and whatsapp queued when limits grant them

evidence.description: documents that add-on charging is not wired to the gateway

blockers: Offline integration run is blocked because target dependencies are not installed
Whether the operator accepts the documented limitation or sells add-ons out of band

validation_plan.local: Run the existing add-on tests offline with dependencies present and confirm activation succeeds with NODE_ENV=production and no payment provider.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner confirms how add-ons are billed in production and whether SMS/WhatsApp providers are configured.

title: Business-product manager gains owner-only employees.manage through module-name collision
description: At registration the manager role receives "<module>.*" for every entity module of the product. The Business product has an entity whose module is "employees", the same namespace as the core permission employees.manage. hasPermission treats employees.* as granting employees.manage, so a manager can create and suspend staff accounts.
root_cause: Product module names share a flat namespace with core permission keys, and wildcard expansion in hasPermission matches by the first dot segment.
intended_behavior: Manager holds only employees.read (SYSTEM_ROLES); creating and suspending login accounts is owner-only.

trace.description: manager gets <module>.* for each product entity
inserts a user and membership with chosen role and password

conditions.description: Attacker holds an authenticated manager session
Tenant registered with the business product

execution.attacker_perspective: Manager of a Business-product tenant using dummy data
instructions: Copy business.ts and packages/shared into an offline sandbox scratch directory
Build manager permissions with the app.ts:93-99 expression
Evaluate the guard used by requirePermission for employees.read and employees.manage
execution.observed_result: managerHasWildcard=true; employees.manage is the only permission escalated beyond baseline; guard result true for manager. Employee role and other owner-only permissions (roles.manage, tenant.settings, subscription.manage) stayed false. HTTP route not executed because dependencies are unavailable offline.

remediation.strategy: Do not derive permission keys from product module names without a namespace. Prefix product permissions (for example "mod:employees.*") or rename the module, and make hasPermission wildcard apply only to the same namespace. Add a regression test for every product that manager lacks employees.manage. Ready-made fix in fix/: business-module-rename.patch (module employees -> hr), migrate-business-manager-permission.sql for existing tenants, and manager-employees.test.ts (copy to apps/api/test/) which fails before the fix and passes after.

likelihood.reason: Needs a manager account in a Business tenant.

impact.reason: Manager can create manager accounts and suspend other non-owner staff; owner cannot be touched.

confidence.reason: Function-level harness observed; route chain verified by source only; no independent verifier agent was available.

title: Plan change applies a higher tier immediately without payment or proration
description: change-plan only checks that access is full and that downgrade usage fits. A tenant may switch to a higher tier for the paid period and switch back before renewal.
claimed_root_cause: Plan change is not tied to a paid invoice for the target tier.

evidence.description: access full includes trialing, active and past_due
billing model for plan changes is not described as prorated

blockers: Intended billing semantics for mid-period upgrades are not in source
Offline integration run blocked by missing dependencies

validation_plan.local: Run platform.test.ts change-plan cases offline and observe limits after upgrade without a new invoice.
validation_plan.deployment: Product owner confirms whether upgrades are meant to bill immediately.

title: Password-reset and verification links may use a client-supplied forwarded host
description: The API builds the emailed reset link from the raw X-Forwarded-Host header when PUBLIC_WEB_URL is unset. An attacker who can reach the API directly could point a victim reset link to an attacker host.
claimed_root_cause: base() trusts req.get("x-forwarded-host") regardless of the trust-proxy setting.

trace.description: link with signed token is emailed

evidence.description: Next proxy overwrites x-forwarded-host with Host or a validated tenant slug
Caddy routes only the configured domain

blockers: Whether port 4000 is reachable from untrusted clients (systemd or pm2 deployments)
Whether PUBLIC_WEB_URL is set in production

validation_plan.local: Run the account-recovery tests offline with a dummy request carrying X-Forwarded-Host and PUBLIC_WEB_URL unset, and read the queued outbox link.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner checks listening sockets and firewall for the API port, and confirms PUBLIC_WEB_URL is set.
